author: Joseph Conrad
title: Heart of Darkness, in Youth: a Narrative, and Two Other Stories
edition: Edinburgh and London: William Blackwood and Sons, 1902. Scan-backed Wikisource transcription. Source HTML navigation and page-number anchors excluded; paragraph line-wrapping and HTML whitespace collapsed to spaces; invisible page-break markers removed. Wording, punctuation and paragraph boundaries retained. The library text holds the whole volume's three stories in printed order: Youth, Heart of Darkness (sections I to III) and The End of the Tether (sections I to XIV), each under its printed title and section numerals; the volume's front matter and the story half-titles are omitted. The row of eight asterisks that divides Youth is kept as one paragraph. A Wikisource editor’s signature found inside the transcription of Youth is removed (see acquisition). Youth (blocks 0-126) was collated word by word against the page images of this 1902 scan (Internet Archive youthnarrativetw00conrrich, the source of the Commons file) on 2026-11-18: its Wikisource transcription follows a later, American-spelled text rather than the scan, so every difference was decided on the page image and the print’s reading adopted (84 replacements): spellings (caulk, recaulked, lustre, smouldered, centre, axe, odours, sombre, travelling, whirr, manœuvring, barque, viâ, 14-foot, every one, some one, a while), words (seem, Accordingly, things, to take charge, rose, fierce, language, round; again, the and a second “too soon” restored; a “with” and a doubled “second” at the page 16-17 join removed), compounds (chin-strap, daresay, scrollwork, steam-colliers, force-pump, jury-rig, a-month; byword, mainyard, coalheavers, underwriters, backbone), and punctuation, including Mrs without a point and the print’s spaced dots for the transcription’s ellipsis character. Heart of Darkness (blocks 127-329) was collated the same way on 2026-11-18, every difference decided on the page images: its transcription follows the same later text, and 287 of its readings are replaced by the print’s. They are spellings (realise, civilised, colour, honour, clamour, lustre, sombre, travelling, woollen, grey, manœuvred, impostor, dumfounded, vermuths and the like); words (marshes, round, clear, desk, flushed, wagged, float, lounged, whole, Tower, lone, black, quick, these, unextinguishable, “I did my possible”, “the murmurs of wild crowds”, “she said” and “she murmured” in the last scene, and others); omissions restored (“Equator, and in every sort of latitude all over the two”, “between the stones, imposing carriage archways”, “Principles?”, and the single words over, on (twice), of, as, him, the (twice), cold, had and like); words the print lacks removed (only, an empty, the, we, that); compounds (river-side, pin-heads, to-day, by-and-by, sandbanks, look-out, summing-up, sandal-wise and others; at two line-end hyphens, bed-place and down-stream follow the print’s bed-place and up-stream elsewhere); and punctuation, chiefly the print’s “too” without commas and its comma before a dash. Throughout Heart of Darkness the print’s Mr without a point (52), its spaced dots for the transcription’s ellipsis character (8) and curly quotation marks for 53 stray straight ones are adopted; of the transcription’s 237 en dashes, 234 in compounds become hyphens and three become the print’s em dashes, and two horizontal bars become em dashes. Two evident printing faults are not reproduced: “Goverment” (p. 140) is given as Government, and the semicolon after “She stood up”, which failed to print (p. 179), is kept. The End of the Tether is not collated; scope.collated limits readings to Youth and Heart of Darkness.

rights.basis: The supplied English text is from the 1902 Blackwood edition, published before 1931 and in the US public domain as of 2026. The digitized volume identifies its publication year; no modern introduction or annotation is included.

acquisition.method: Wikisource rendered page HTML (index.php action=render) for twenty pages in printed order: Youth: a Narrative, and Two Other Stories/Youth, /Heart of Darkness and its /Section 1 to /Section 3, /The End of the Tether and its /Section 1 to /Section 14 (revisions 10698534, 16458211, 10698120, 10698223, 10698217, 10698221, 10698236, 10698257, 10698274, 10698306, 10698321, 10698344, 10698366, 10698377, 10698420, 10698443, 10698495, 10698494, 10698531, 10698569); downloadSha256 is the SHA-256 of the twenty responses concatenated in that order and downloadUrl the first of them. Only the transcluded scan text is used: Wikisource headers, page-number anchors and zero-width page-boundary characters removed (the transcription has no footnotes); half-title pages dropped; story titles and section numerals became headings; the asterisk line-separator table became one paragraph of spaced asterisks; paragraphs joined with whitespace and the transcription's hard line breaks collapsed; emphasis flattened. A Wikisource editor’s signature, “19Eliza (talk) 02:12, 3 December 2023 (UTC)”, left inside the transcluded text of Youth between “Bless the old woman.” and “She overhauled my outfit”, is removed (2026-11-18). Youth was then compared word by word with the Internet Archive OCR of the same scan (youthnarrativetw00conrrich_djvu.txt) after whitespace normalisation, each difference read on the Commons page image, and the print’s reading adopted (84 replacements, listed in edition; 2026-11-18). Heart of Darkness was then compared the same way with the same OCR, each difference read on the Commons page image, and the print’s reading adopted (287 replacements, with the typographic normalisations summarised in edition; 2026-11-18). The End of the Tether remains as transcribed.
